hard_separation.civic_preparation: Universal obligation to prepare every young person for citizenship.
hard_separation.suffrage: Franchise eligibility is a legal/democratic design question — never an examination, certification, GPA, service-hour, or political-knowledge gate.

hypotheses.text: Under identifiable institutional conditions — especially local decision-making, civic education, and dense civic networks — extending suffrage to 16- and 17-year-olds for local elections may strengthen meaningful and durable civic participation without requiring civic tests, certifications, academic achievement, service hours, or political-knowledge prerequisites for the franchise.
hypotheses.central_question: Under what institutional conditions does enfranchisement at 16 produce meaningful, durable civic participation?
hypotheses.sequencing_note: Prior 'education first then suffrage' preference is now an explicit testable question — not locked doctrine.
hypotheses.obsolete_framing_rejected: Complete civics certification / pass a test / finish service hours to earn the ballot at 16.
hypotheses.failure_mode_case: Newark NJ school-board 2025 (rights without repaired civic culture)

governance.reason: Upgrade to serious comparative empirical track with Maryland labs, Newark contrary evidence, Brattleboro, and international cases. Not a principle. Not locked policy.
